## Summary

Qingdao Hisense Communications was established in 2001 within the
Hisense group to make mobile phones and has a technical cooperation
with Qualcomm [2]. Hisense, headquartered in Qingdao, grew from the
Qingdao No. 2 Radio Factory of 1969 and makes TVs, white goods,
set-top boxes and phones, with Gorenje, Toshiba Visual Solutions and
the VIDAA smart-TV platform among its holdings [2]. The IEEE registry
lists 13 MA-L blocks to Qingdao Hisense Communications Co.,Ltd., almost
all at Qianwangang Road 218, Qingdao [1]; Hisense's TV, broadband and
appliance companies hold their own blocks under other names and are not
this entry [1].

A MAC in these blocks is most likely a Hisense phone: Hisense sells
budget and mid-tier Android phones and e-ink devices, is a major phone
maker in Mexico and South Africa, and sold phones in Indonesia under
Smartfren's Andromax brand [2]. That those phones carry this
registrant's blocks is inferred from the company's role, not stated
by a source [1][2]. NVD lists pre-installed app flaws on the Hisense
U965 and F17 Android phones [3][4]. Radios, chipsets, FCC grantee codes
and randomisation are not listed: the FCC ID databases and web search
were unavailable to the session that wrote this entry, and nothing is
filled in from memory [1].
